spec.name: Nostromo Galley
spec.description: A retro-futuristic spaceship mess and galley corner from the USCSS Nostromo (Alien, 1979): ribbed bone-coloured walls, a cream counter with beverage and warming equipment, a wall bank of glowing CRT monitors, the iconic molded mess table with attached stools, and a bristling ceiling of pipes and conduit over a steel deck.
spec.layout: A cut-away room section: the viewer looks in through the open +Z face. A steel deck plate floor covers the whole footprint and rests on y = 0 (only floor-touching part). The back wall (z = -2.5) carries the galley: a counter run 0.95 m high with equipment, and above it a wall-mounted CRT monitor bank. The left wall (x = -2.3) carries lockers and stacked storage crates; the right wall (x = +2.3) carries a ribbed panel section and a round pressure hatch. A ceiling slab closes the top with pipes, conduit runs and two cone lamps hanging over the mess table, which stands centre-front with its cluster of attached swivel stools. Style on every part: warm bone and cream molded-plastic surfaces like airliner interiors, dark olive-grey machinery, corrugated ribbing on every flat wall, warning-yellow stripe accents, rust and copper fittings, amber and green glowing CRT screens, everything chunky, functional and 1979-industrial.

parts.builds: The room section itself. Steel deck floor of rectangular plates with seam grooves, a raised grating strip near the back, all in floor colour with rust stains and a warning-yellow painted stripe across the doorway end. Three walls: back wall, left wall, right wall, built as chunky ribbed panel walls — flat wall-coloured panels with repeated vertical rib slats in rib colour, dark seam lines, corner posts in iron, a black kick skirting at the bottom and a pipe-and-conduit raceway band at mid height with small valve wheels in brass and rust. The right wall holds a round pressure hatch: lathe-built ring, rivet ring, spokes, a warning-yellow and black chevron stripe band around it and a small stencil-style plate. The ceiling slab closes the top with recessed panel frames and two square light-well openings the ceiling-services part drops into. Wall edges frame the open +Z face with a thick girder border so the cut-away reads as a ship section.
parts.attaches: Owns the whole footprint; its floor top is mount deckTop that galleyCounter, messTable and lockersShelf stand on; its back wall face is mount backWallFace for galleyCounter and monitorBank; its left wall face is mount leftWallFace for lockersShelf; its ceiling underside is mount ceilingLine for ceilingServices.

parts.builds: Everything under the ceiling: a dense overhead services run. Two large parallel copper pipes (pipeCopper) running front-to-back with flanged ring joints every metre and elbow bends, a bundle of steel conduit pipes (pipeSteel) in a cable tray, a smaller olive cable duct, hanging black cable loops with clip rings, and two cone pendant lamps in iron hanging on short stems over the mess table position, each with a glowing warm lampGlow shade disc. Add a small junction box in machine grey with an orange stripe, a hanging hose reel with a coiled rubber hose, and riveted mounting brackets in iron connecting everything to mount ceilingLine. Pipes must not drop below y = 2.05 so the room stays open.
parts.attaches: Hangs from mount ceilingLine on the roomShell ceiling underside; its lamp cones hang above the messTable footprint.

parts.builds: The galley counter run along the back wall, standing on mount deckTop and backing onto mount backWallFace. A machine-grey cabinet base with cream cabinet doors (thin seam gaps, small black pulls), a chunky ivory worktop with a raised lip, and equipment across it: a tall beverage dispenser tower in chalk with an orange stripe band, two brass dispensing nozzles and a small drip tray; a countertop warming oven with a dark glass door, rust handle and amber indicator jewel lights; a sink recess with a steel tap and drying rack; a wall shelf above the worktop holding mugs and canisters in olive, rust and chalk. A tiled-ish backsplash strip in machine grey with a warning-yellow stripe, a rubber floor mat in front, and a small wall-mounted extinguisher in rust. Details read as seated parts: indicator lights, valve knobs, seams, stripe bands each their own colour.
parts.attaches: Stands on mount deckTop, backs onto mount backWallFace; its worktop height 1.2 m leaves clear wall above for monitorBank.

parts.builds: The wall-mounted monitor console above the galley counter, meeting mount backWallFace. An iron mounting frame bolted to the wall carries a bank of four CRT screens in dark casings: two larger green glowing screens with scanline frames and surrounding bezels, one amber glowing screen, one small amber data readout, all with glow (self-lit) treatment on the screen faces only. Below and beside the screens: a chunky control panel in machine grey with rows of chunky switches (black toggles with orange and warning-coloured caps), push buttons in brass and rust, and a stencil-style data placard. Cable ducts in black run from the frame into the wall, and a small reel of coiled cable hangs at one end. Everything sits between y 1.35 and 2.15, clear of the counter below.
parts.attaches: Bolts onto mount backWallFace above the galleyCounter worktop line; nothing below y 1.35 so the counter's shelf clears it.

parts.builds: The iconic Nostromo mess table, centre-front, standing on mount deckTop. A chunky ivory molded table top (rounded octagon-ish slab, tabletop colour) on a heavy dark iron pedestal base with a ribbed column and a round foot. Around it, six attached-style swivel stools: each a molded beige stool seat (stool colour) on a slim dark column with a weighted black base, arranged around the table at varied heights and slight rotations so it feels lived-in. On the table: small cream cups, a metal tray with recessed eating compartments, a small brass ashtray, a lidded beaker, and a pack of cards fan in chalk with black pips. A floor mat in rubber under the stool cluster. Keep the silhouette bold and readable from the front view.
parts.attaches: Stands on mount deckTop in the open centre of the room; its stools stay inside its box, clear of the counter at z < -1.45.

parts.builds: Left-wall storage against mount leftWallFace, standing on mount deckTop. A row of four tall crew lockers in olive with cream door frames, vent slats in black, small number plates and black latches; above them a wall-mounted rack of equipment cases in orange and rust with warning-yellow stripes. Beside the lockers a floor-standing stack: two olive supply crates with stencil-style plates and strap bands, a small drum in machine grey with a rust ring, and a few individually placed props — a black toolbox with a brass clasp, a stack of metal ration tins in chalk and machine grey, a hanging clip lamp in iron with a warm lampGlow bulb. All details (slats, plates, latches, bands) as small parts in their own colours.
parts.attaches: Stands on mount deckTop and backs onto mount leftWallFace on the roomShell's left wall; keeps its right face at x = -1.15 clear of the messTable.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec JSON for a spaceship galley kitchen in Alien (1979) Nostromo style. The Nostromo's galley is famous: the long table with raw eggs? Actually the iconic scene is the crew eating breakfast around the table, and the alien emerging. The galley has: white/cream plastic molded chairs and table, muted industrial interiors, retro-futuristic CRT screens, amber/green monitors, pipes, corrugated walls, storage lockers, coffee machine, hanging lamps.

The model: a galley kitchen corner/section of the Nostromo. Elements: table with attached stools, galley counter with equipment, wall panels with CRT monitors, pipes on the ceiling, a hatch, lockers, a coffee/beverage dispenser. Retro-futuristic 1979 industrial: beige/off-white molded furniture, muted olive/brown tones, corrugated ribbed walls, warning stripes, CRT amber screens.

Size: it's a prop group — a room section. Maybe 4.2 m wide, 2.6 m tall, 5 m long. Stands on floor y=0.

Parts (3-6): 
1. deck and walls / room shell (floor plates, ribbed wall panels, ceiling with pipes) — floor true.
2. galley counter block with equipment (dispenser, sink, warming oven, knobs, lights).
3. mess table with attached stools (the iconic Nostromo mess table).
4. monitor wall / terminal console with CRT screens (glowing).
5. ceiling truss with pipes and hanging lamps? Could combine with walls.

Static model: joints = [] likely, but maybe a couple of hinge joints for a hatch? Keep it static — "joints": []. Actually maybe give a couple of joints for a screen or a door? Static models may omit joints entirely. Keep static for simplicity.

Mounts: floorDeck [0,0.25,0] where counter and table stand; wallLine? Counter attaches to wall at back. Table on floor.

Let me define size: [4.6, 2.7, 5.0]. Room section: floor, back wall (at -z?), walls. The front faces +Z — so the open side is +Z (viewer looks in). Back wall at z=-2.5.

Boxes:
- shell (deck + walls + ceiling): x [-2.3,2.3], y [0,2.7], z [-2.5,2.5]. floor: true.
- counter run along the back wall: x [-2.3,2.3]? Counter could run along left wall. Let's put counter along the back wall (z from -2.5 to -1.6), x from -2.2 to 2.2, y 0 to 1.0 (counter top at ~0.95). Hmm, but the monitor wall also on back wall — put monitors above counter (y 1.2-2.2). Or monitors on left wall.

Let me plan the room:
- Back wall (z = -2.5) has the galley counter with equipment, and above it monitors/CRT.
- Left wall (x = -2.3): lockers and cabinets.
- Right wall (x = +2.3): doorway/hatch? Maybe ribbed panels + hatch.
- Ceiling: pipes and conduit running, hanging cone lamps.
- Mess table in the middle-front, with the iconic attached swivel stools.

Parts:
1. `roomShell` — floor plates, ribbed walls, ceiling, hatch on right wall, wall trims, warning stripes. Budget ~220.
2. `pipeCeiling` — could merge into shell. Better split: ceiling pipes & conduit & lamps as one part (the "services"). x [-2.3,2.3], y [1.9,2.7], z [-2.5,2.5]. Budget ~140.
3. `galleyCounter` — counter along back wall: cabinets, worktop, beverage dispenser, warming cabinet, sink, controls, amber lights, coffee urn. y 0-1.15, z [-2.5,-1.5]. Budget ~200.
4. `monitorBank` — wall-mounted CRT console above counter plus side terminal: glowing green/amber screens, casings, switches. y [1.2,2.1], z [-2.5,-2.1]. Budget ~150.
5. `messTable` — table + stools, iconic. Center-front: x [-1.6,1.6], y [0,1.0], z [-0.8,1.6]. Budget ~180.
6. `lockersShelf` — left wall lockers + storage crates, kettle props? x [-2.3,-1.2], y [0,2.3], z [-1.2,2.2]. Budget ~130.

Total: 220+140+200+150+180+130 = 1020. Too much; cap at 900. Trim: shell 200, services 120, counter 190, monitors 140, table 180, lockers 110 = 940. Trim to 200+110+180+140+170+100 = 900. Good.

Mounts: 
- `deck` [0, 0.25, 0] — raised floor plate top where furniture stands? Or floor at y=0. Let floor plates be thin, top at y=0.06. Mount deckTop [0, 0.06, 0].
- `wallBack` [0, 1.2, -2.5]? Counter attaches to back wall: mount backWallFace [0, 0, -2.5] plane. Simpler: mounts are points: `counterFootline` [0, 0.06, -2.45], `counterTop` [0, 1.15, -2.0] where monitors sit above.
- `tableDeck` [0,0.06,0.4].
- `ceilingLine` [0, 2.7, 0] — services attach to ceiling.

Mounts required: every place two parts touch has a mount. So:
- deckTop: [0, 0.06, 0] — floor surface (shell owns floor; counter, table, lockers stand on it).
- backWall: [0, 1.25, -2.44] — where counter & monitor bank meet the shell's back wall.
- leftWall: [-2.28, 1.15, 0.5] — lockers against left wall.
- ceiling: [0, 2.66, 0] — services attach to ceiling.

Palette (max 24): Nostromo colours: off-white/beige plastic, warm grey walls, olive drab, dark iron, amber CRT glow, green screen glow, warning yellow, rust orange, copper pipes, black rubber, cream molded seats.
